name: Abaddon
desc: Places Scarab Hives that periodically spawn scarabs to seek out and attack nearby enemies and beds.
adv: Each hive spawns scarabs that hunt down enemies and beds. Scarabs attack every 0.5 seconds. Scarabs from the same hive do not stack their damage, so two scarabs from one hive deal the same DPS as one. Scarabs from different hives do stack, so two hives can hit you twice as hard, and three hives deal up to 3x the DPS. Hives are weak to pickaxes and break in 5 hits with a wooden pickaxe, 4 with stone, and 2 with iron or diamond. When a hive expires or is broken, its scarabs take about 10 damage. Scarab upgrades and Hive upgrades are bought separately.

items.name: Scarab Upgrade 1
items.desc: Scarabs deal 4 damage and have 165 HP. Scarabs can now fly and climb blocks to reach enemies.

items.name: Hive Upgrade 1
items.desc: Hive lasts 15 seconds and spawns 4 scarabs in total.

items.name: Scarab Upgrade 2
items.desc: Scarabs deal 6 damage, have 190 HP, and move faster. An exploding scarab with 100 HP spawns alongside the 4th scarab, with the same damage and block destruction as TNT.

items.name: Hive Upgrade 2
items.desc: Hive lasts 18 seconds and spawns a scarab every 3.5 seconds, 6 in total. An exploding scarab spawns with the 4th one, making 7 in total.

items.name: Scarab Upgrade 3
items.desc: Scarabs deal 8 damage and have 220 HP. Every time a scarab hits an enemy, you heal 1 HP.

items.name: Hive Upgrade 3
items.desc: Hive still lasts 18 seconds. Each spawn has a 25% chance to spawn an extra scarab. An exploding scarab still spawns with the 4th one.

abilities.name: Place Hive
abilities.desc: Places a Scarab Hive that spawns scarabs. Base (Tier 0): scarabs have 140 HP and deal 2 damage. The hive lasts 12 seconds and spawns a scarab every 4.5 seconds, 3 in total. You get a new hive every 20 seconds, holding up to 2.

passives.name: Hive Supply
passives.desc: You receive a new Scarab Hive every 20 seconds and can hold up to 2 at a time.

passives.name: Scarab Climbing
passives.desc: Scarabs can fly and climb blocks to reach enemies.

passives.name: Scarab Lifesteal
passives.desc: Every time a scarab hits an enemy, you heal 1 HP.

strategy.title: Protect your hives
strategy.text: Enemies can break hives quickly, so place them up high or hide them where they are hard to reach.

strategy.title: Let scarabs tank for you
strategy.text: Use your scarabs as a shield: they soak up hits while you fight.

balWhy: The hives are easily broken and a bit expensive, but it provides good value if you know how to play it.

counter.title: Fireballs and hive breaking
counter.text: Use fireballs, or break the hive before it spawns any more bugs.

changes: Hive duration increased by 2s at every level
Scarab health now only starts decreasing once the spawner disappears or moves out of range
Scarab & Hive first level upgrade cost: 80 iron → 40 iron

name: Adetunde
desc: Start with a powerful Frosty Hammer. Hitting enemies has a chance to drop Frost Crystals, which you can spend to upgrade your hammer.
adv:
You spawn with a Frosty Hammer, which has a 4.5 block reach, the same as a sword. Every hit on an enemy has an 80% chance to give you a Frost Crystal. Crystals are spent on hammer upgrades, can be stored in your Personal Chest, and are all lost when you die.
Tier 1 costs 3 crystals (9 in total), Tier 2 costs 7 crystals (21 in total), and Tier 3 costs 15. The upgrades are Speed, Shield and Damage, and you can only pick one Tier 3 upgrade. Every time you upgrade, you are frozen in place for 2 seconds.
Shield is capped at 50. If you have not hit anyone for 2 seconds, it drops by 5 every 0.75 seconds.
The Tier 3 upgrade you pick gives you something special: Damage unlocks the Arctic Slam ability, Shield unlocks the Permafrost Shield ability, and Speed (cooldown) unlocks the Blizzard Storm passive.

items.name: Frosty Hammer
items.desc: Your main weapon, with a 4.5 block reach, the same as a sword. Tier 0 deals 23 damage every 0.35 seconds. Each hit has an 80% chance to drop a Frost Crystal.

items.name: Frost Crystal
items.desc: Gained from hitting enemies (80% chance). Spend them on hammer upgrades or store them in your Personal Chest. You lose all of them when you die.

abilities.name: Open Hammer Upgrades
abilities.desc:
Opens the hammer upgrade menu. Each upgrade freezes you in place for 2 seconds.
Tier 0: 23 damage every 0.35 seconds.
Tier 1 (3 crystals): 30 damage every 0.32 seconds, and 2 shield per attack.
Tier 2 (7 crystals): 40 damage every 0.28 seconds, and 3 shield per attack.
Tier 3 (15 crystals, pick one): 52 damage, or 4 shield per attack, or a 0.25 second cooldown. Each one unlocks its own ability or passive.

abilities.name: Permafrost Shield
abilities.desc: Gain 30 shield for 6 seconds. The shield then explodes in a 7 block radius, dealing damage based on how much shield you have. The explosion has 100% armor penetration.

abilities.name: Arctic Slam
abilities.desc: Hits 3 times over 2 seconds for 40, then 30, then 20 damage (90 in total). Each hit has 10% armor penetration. Reaches a 20 block radius, 9 blocks wide from end to end and 3 blocks tall. Damages and breaks blocks depending on their type, and launches enemies 2 blocks into the air.

passives.name: Frost Crystal Drops
passives.desc: 80% chance to gain a Frost Crystal. Crystals are lost on death, but you can keep them safe in your Personal Chest.

passives.name: Upgrade Freeze
passives.desc: You are frozen in place for 2 seconds every time you upgrade your hammer.

passives.name: Shield Decay
passives.desc: Shield is capped at 50 and drops by 5 every 0.75 seconds.

passives.name: Blizzard Storm
passives.desc: After landing 4 hits in a row, an aura with a 6 block radius forms around you. It ticks every 0.525 seconds, starting at 3 damage and rising by 1 per tick up to a max of 8. The longer you keep hitting, the longer the aura lasts after you stop: every hit adds 1 extra tick.

strategy.title: Hit and run early
strategy.text: Your hammer has a slow cooldown at first, so use hit-and-run tactics to collect crystals safely. Save them up before upgrading your cooldown, then your damage.

strategy.title: Upgrade order
strategy.text: Always keep upgrading, and take Cooldown and Damage before Shield.

strategy.title: Best Tier 3 pick
strategy.text: Tier 3 Damage gives the best DPS. You can choose the others if you prefer them or want to play that specific style.

strategy.title: Arctic Slam on bridges
strategy.text: Use Arctic Slam when enemies are crossing bridges. It destroys the bridge and drops them into the void.

balWhy: You save a ton of resources that would normally go into your sword just by upgrading the hammer, and how hard it is to upgrade is part of the cost.

counter.title: Limit its hits
counter.text: Don't let it get many hits on you.

counter.title: Don't let it escape
counter.text: If it is close to its final upgrade, don't let it get away, or it will chest all of its crystals.

name: Aery
desc: Killing enemies adds to your collection of spirit butterflies. Each spirit butterfly amplifies sword and projectile damage. Aery's base health is reduced by 10%.
adv:
Aery spawns with 90 HP. You gain 2 butterflies for every kill, and none for assists. Each butterfly is one stack, and stacks increase your projectile damage by 80% of the butterfly's value.
The bonus slows down as you collect more: each new stack adds less damage than the last, and eventually each butterfly adds less than 1 damage. After killing an enemy, you have to wait 25 seconds before you can gain stacks from that same enemy again.
When you die you lose part of your stacks, and the more stacks you have, the bigger the share you lose (see the stack loss table).

calc.title: Stack calculator
calc.label: Butterfly stacks
calc.note: Bonus damage from butterfly stacks. The listed values are exact; other numbers use the formula damage = 2.0104 × stacks^0.7144.

passives.name: Butterfly Stacks
passives.desc: Gain 2 butterflies for every kill. Assists give none. Each butterfly is one stack.

passives.name: Butterfly Damage
passives.desc: Increases your projectile damage by 80% of the butterfly's value. Each extra stack adds less than the last, eventually under 1 damage per butterfly.

passives.name: Same-Enemy Cooldown
passives.desc: You cannot gain stacks from the same enemy again for 25 seconds.

passives.name: Stack Loss
passives.desc: You lose 15% of your stacks with 0–9 stacks, 20% with 10–19, 25% with 20–29, and 33% with 30 or more.

strategy.title: Get support early
strategy.text: Aery needs help early in the game to build up stacks. Around 20 stacks is the sweet spot.

strategy.title: Don't ego fights
strategy.text: Losing stacks hurts, so avoid fights you don't need to take.

strategy.title: Go ranged at 20 stacks
strategy.text: Once you reach 20 stacks, switch to ranged weapons so you don't risk losing all your stacks late in the game.

balWhy: Many people use it, and even though it may be slightly outclassed, it still has a use because it works great with support.

counter.title: Be prepared
counter.text: Don't fight it if you are unprepared, and warn your teammates.

name: Agni
desc: Throw cluster bombs at your enemies and watch them go flying! Blast off with your Rocket Boost ability.
adv:
Agni's kit is built around fire and explosives. Fire deals 3 damage per tick for 3 ticks, 9 damage in total.
Rocket Boost launches you into the air and burns enemies it hits. Cluster Bombs are thrown at enemies and burst into smaller fire bombs that spread out and explode. Throwing a Cluster Bomb takes 2 seconds from start to finish.

items.name: Cluster Bomb
items.desc: You get a new Cluster Bomb every 35 seconds, holding up to 5, or you can buy one in the shop. The bomb deals 16-17 damage and applies Fire. It then drops 8 smaller fire bombs in a 25 block radius. Each one explodes in a 3x3 area, dealing 12 damage and applying Fire. Throwing it takes 2 seconds in total.

abilities.name: Rocket Boost
abilities.desc: Launches you up to 7 blocks into the air. Deals 12 damage to enemies and applies Fire (3 damage per tick, 3 ticks).

strategy.title: Save your iron
strategy.text: Don't waste early-game iron on Cluster Bombs. Only buy them when you have plenty of iron left over.

strategy.title: When to throw them
strategy.text: Use Cluster Bombs in group fights, and always use one when you have to fight someone one-on-one.

strategy.title: Rocket Boost tricks
strategy.text: Use Rocket Boost to save yourself from fall damage, or to deal extra damage to your enemy.

balWhy: It just doesn't do a lot of damage compared to similar kits that spawn an item every few seconds, and the Rocket Boost jump is pretty situational.

counter.title: Bait the jump
counter.text: Try to bait it into using Rocket Boost near you so it misses.

name: Alchemist
desc: Use flasks to brew various potions with foraged ingredients.
adv:
Thorns, Mushrooms and Flowers spawn frequently around the map. You can pick up all of them, and drop them or store them in a chest. The same goes for the potions you make, but not the flasks.
You can buy Alchemist Flasks in the shop for 10 iron, with a max of 16. While holding a flask, add Thorns, Mushrooms and Flowers to brew a special potion:
3 Mushrooms: Sleep Splash Potion
3 Flowers: Heal Splash Potion
1 Thorn + 2 Mushrooms: Poison Splash Potion
2 Thorns + 1 Flower: Big Shield

items.name: Alchemist Flask
items.desc: Buy up to 16 in the shop. While holding it, add Thorns, Mushrooms and Flowers to brew special potions. Flasks cannot be stored in a chest.

items.name: Mushroom
items.desc: Spawns frequently around the map. Used for Sleep and Poison potions. Can be picked up, dropped and stored in a chest.

items.name: Thorn
items.desc: Spawns frequently around the map. Used for Poison potions and Big Shields. Can be picked up, dropped and stored in a chest.

items.name: Flower
items.desc: Spawns frequently around the map. Used for Heal potions and Big Shields. Can be picked up, dropped and stored in a chest.

items.name: Sleep Splash Potion
items.desc: Stuns anyone hit, including you, for 2 seconds in a 3x3 block radius.

items.name: Heal Splash Potion
items.desc: Heals 30 HP in a 5x5 block radius.

items.name: Poison Splash Potion
items.desc: Deals 6 damage per tick for 10 ticks, with 80% armor penetration. Poison cannot kill: it leaves enemies on 1 HP at minimum.

items.name: Big Shield
items.desc: Gives you 30 shield.

abilities.name: Add Thorns
abilities.desc: Adds a Thorn to the flask. Used in the Poison Splash Potion (1 Thorn) and Big Shield (2 Thorns) recipes.

abilities.name: Add Mushroom
abilities.desc: Adds a Mushroom to the flask. Used in the Sleep Splash Potion (3 Mushrooms) and Poison Splash Potion (2 Mushrooms) recipes.

abilities.name: Add Flowers
abilities.desc: Adds a Flower to the flask. Used in the Heal Splash Potion (3 Flowers) and Big Shield (1 Flower) recipes.

passives.name: Foraging
passives.desc: Thorns, Mushrooms and Flowers spawn frequently around the map. You can pick up, drop and store them in a chest.

strategy.title: Craft for your playstyle
strategy.text: Choose which potions to craft depending on how you play.

strategy.title: Solo and offensive play
strategy.text: Mainly craft Heal and Sleep potions, so you can stunlock enemies and keep yourself healthy.

strategy.title: Supporting your team
strategy.text: Craft Big Shields and Heal potions for your teammates, and Sleep and Poison potions for yourself to help in fights.

strategy.title: Always be prepared
strategy.text: Use a Shield potion before every fight, and have a Poison potion ready to throw. Prioritize keeping 1 Poison potion and 1 Shield potion on hand, and always keep crafting Heal potions and Shields.

balWhy: Even though not many people use it, stunlocking people is not healthy game design. It might need a nerf in that area, with buffs elsewhere to balance it out.

counter.title: Keep building
counter.text: It can stunlock you very easily, so keep building to mess up its aim.

counter.title: Waste its healing
counter.text: Use ranged weapons to make it waste all of its healing.

name: Arachne
desc: The Spider Queen uses web bridges to traverse the map and can summon spiderlings from her webs to attack enemies. Enemies are slowed if they run into her webs.
adv:
Arachne shoots webs that slow enemies down and double as a bridge only you and your Arachne teammates can use. Enemies who touch cobwebs are slowed by a lot, and the more cobwebs they touch, the slower they get.
You can summon spiders while you have webs placed. You get 1 to 4 spiders depending on how many cobwebs are up, so 1 cobweb gives 1 spider and 4 or more cobwebs give 4. Spiders disappear after 6 seconds. Each spider spawns with 30 HP and deals 4 damage every 0.5 seconds. When a spider kills or assists on an enemy, its damage and HP go up, to a max of 80 HP and 15 damage.

abilities.name: Aim Web Bridge
abilities.desc: Shoots a web in any direction with a 17 block line radius. Enemies who touch the cobwebs are slowed by a lot, and the slow builds up the more cobwebs they touch. You can jump onto the cobwebs and use them as a bridge, but only you and other Arachne teammates can use it.

abilities.name: Spider Summon
abilities.desc: Summons 1 to 4 spiders from your webs, depending on how many cobwebs are up (1 cobweb = 1 spider, 4 or more = 4). Spiders last 6 seconds before they disappear. Each spider spawns with 30 HP and deals 4 damage every 0.5 seconds. A spider that kills or assists on an enemy gains damage and HP, up to 80 HP and 15 damage.

passives.name: Sticky Webs
passives.desc: Enemies are slowed by a lot, and the slow gets stronger the more cobwebs they touch.

passives.name: Spider Growth
passives.when: When a spider kills or assists
passives.desc: The spider's damage and HP increase, up to a max of 80 HP and 15 damage. Spiders spawn with 30 HP and 4 damage.

strategy.title: Move fast and save iron
strategy.text: Use Arachne for movement, and save a ton of iron you would normally spend on blocks.

strategy.title: Grab loot first
strategy.text: On most maps you can use the ability right away and get to the middle for loot before anyone else, depending on the mode.

strategy.title: Slow your enemies
strategy.text: The webs slow enemies down a lot, which gives you a big advantage in PvP.

strategy.title: Let spiders tank
strategy.text: Use your spiders to soak up damage while you fight.

balWhy: Nobody really notices or cares about the spiders leveling up, so that should be removed. Its damage should be improved overall, and it could get some armor penetration as a unique perk.
notes: The webs make people get anti-cheated the second they touch them.

counter.title: Don't touch the webs
counter.text: Touching the webs makes you anti-cheat so badly that it's pretty much an automatic death.

changes: Added timer on when spiders will dissapear
Added stack counter for spider level
Fix spiders not leveling up with assist kills

name: Archer
desc: Can headshot with bows, crossbows and headhunters, which normally can't! Deal 12.5% more projectile damage and gain access to the Tactical Crossbow in the Item Shop.
adv: Normal bows and crossbows can't headshot, but Archer can headshot with the Bow, Crossbow and Headhunter. Archer also deals extra damage with each of them. The Tactical Crossbow and Tactical Headhunter are cheaper for Archer, at 6 emeralds and 21 emeralds. Each weapon's damage, cooldown and bonus over normal damage are listed under Abilities and items.

items.name: Bow
items.desc:
Damage depends on how long you charge it.
Lowest charge: 10 damage (15 headshot), 0.625 second cooldown.
Highest charge: 20 damage (30 headshot), 1 second cooldown.
Bodyshots deal 12.50% more damage than normal, and headshots deal 79.89% more.

items.name: Tactical Crossbow
items.desc:
Cheaper for Archer. Deals 42.75 damage (64 headshot) with a 1.3 second cooldown.
Bodyshots deal 25.74% more damage than normal, and headshots deal 88.59% more.

items.name: Tactical Headhunter
items.desc:
Cheaper for Archer. Deals 67.5 damage (101.25 headshot) with a 1.3 second cooldown.
Bodyshots and headshots both deal 22.73% more damage than normal.

passives.name: Headshots
passives.desc: Archer can headshot with the Bow, Crossbow and Headhunter. Normal bows and crossbows can't headshot.

passives.name: Projectile Bonus
passives.desc: Deals extra damage with the Bow, Crossbow and Headhunter compared to normal. The bonus for each weapon is listed under its item.

passives.name: Cheaper Weapons
passives.desc: The Tactical Crossbow costs 6 emeralds and the Tactical Headhunter costs 21 emeralds.

strategy.title: Aim for headshots
strategy.text: Headshots are the best part of Archer, so always aim for the head.

strategy.title: Save emeralds for the Crossbow
strategy.text: Save the emeralds you get from the middle and buy the Tactical Crossbow as fast as you can. Archer gets the biggest damage increase over a normal crossbow, so it gives you a lot of control.

balWhy: Its damage is worse than every special bow kit, including kits that aren't even in the Ranged class. It needs a unique mechanic instead of more damage, since the headshot gimmick is a bit outdated.

counter.title: Not much counterplay
counter.text: There isn't much counterplay, since no kit has better ranged damage.

counter.title: Deny the middle
counter.text: Don't let it collect the middle emeralds, so it can't get its crossbow early.

changes: Can now headshot with any projectile
+Tactical Headhunter → Deals 8% more damage & costs 10% fewer emeralds than the Headhunter
Removed the regular crossbow from Archer's shop since the Tactical Crossbow is cheaper

name: Ares
desc: A powerful ancient warrior that uses electric-charged throwing spears to destroy his enemies.
adv:
Ares throws electric-charged Spears. You can buy Spears in the shop for 40 iron, holding up to 10, or wait 40 seconds for a free one to generate. Free spears won't generate if you already have 3 or more.
Spears fly slowly, at half the speed of an arrow, but have a massive range. They can hit through walls, and can hit someone above or below a floor or ceiling. They can also hit you, so be careful.
When a Spear hits, it applies Zapped 1 for 5 seconds in a 4x4 block radius, which reduces healing and shields by 40%.

items.name: Spear
items.desc: Buy up to 10 in the shop, or wait 40 seconds for one to generate (it won't generate if you have 3 or more). Deals 40 damage with 40% armor penetration, with a 0.75 second throw cooldown. It has a massive range, but travels at half the speed of an arrow. It can hit through walls and floors or ceilings, and it can hit you. Applies Zapped 1 for 5 seconds in a 4x4 block radius, reducing healing and shields by 40%. Killing someone with it gives you another Spear.

passives.name: Spear Generation
passives.desc: You get a free Spear every 40 seconds. It won't generate if you already have 3 or more Spears.

passives.name: Spear Refund
passives.when: When you kill someone with a Spear
passives.desc: You gain another Spear.

passives.name: Zapped 1
passives.desc: Everyone in a 4x4 block radius, including you, is Zapped for 5 seconds. Healing and shields are reduced by 40%.

strategy.title: Back off and throw
strategy.text: Damage someone first. When they are in range of a Spear, back off and throw it to get another one back.

strategy.title: Spam late game
strategy.text: Once you have a lot of iron later in the game, spam Spears.

strategy.title: Don't hit yourself
strategy.text: The blast can hit you too, so make sure you are outside the 4x4 radius when you throw.

strategy.title: Target healers and shielders
strategy.text: Zapped cuts healing and shields by 40%, so aim at enemies who heal or shield for the best results.

balWhy: It now gets outclassed by other kits, and it needs more armor penetration to make up for all the damage it lost through nerfs.

counter.title: Dodge early spears
counter.text: Early game it won't have many spears, so dodge them by placing blocks and building over them. This baits it into throwing and missing.

counter.title: Fight up close
counter.text: Fight it up close so the spear also hits Ares himself.

name: Axolotl Amy
desc: Use your pet axolotls to empower yourself and nearby teammates with shields, increased attack damage, faster break speed and health regen.
adv:
Buy Axolotls in the shop to power up yourself and nearby teammates. Every Axolotl has a 5 second cooldown and a 9 block radius.
Shield Axolotl gives shield when you are damaged, Damage Axolotl boosts damage after you hit someone, Break Speed Axolotl speeds up block breaking, and Health Regen Axolotl heals you when you drop below 50% HP.

items.name: Shield Axolotl
items.desc: Gives you and nearby teammates 15 shield when they get damaged. 9 block radius.

items.name: Damage Axolotl
items.desc: Gives you and nearby teammates 16% more damage. Activates after you deal damage. 9 block radius.

items.name: Break Speed Axolotl
items.desc: Gives you and nearby teammates 60% break speed. 9 block radius.

items.name: Health Regen Axolotl
items.desc: Heals you and your teammates by 1% HP every 0.55 seconds for 5 seconds (about 9 ticks). Activates when you take damage below 50% HP. 9 block radius.

strategy.title: Shield Axolotl early
strategy.text: Get the Shield Axolotl early in the game and stick with your teammates so they benefit from it too.

strategy.title: Damage Axolotl later
strategy.text: Only buy the Damage Axolotl after you have iron armor and a stone sword.

strategy.title: Break Speed is the strongest
strategy.text: Break Speed Axolotl is the most powerful one. Use it to shred through bed defenses.

strategy.title: Health Regen is expensive
strategy.text: The Health Regen Axolotl costs too much. Only buy it once you have the essentials you need, like a crossbow, diamond armor, enchants and pearls.

balWhy: Some of the prices are outrageous for what the Axolotls do. The prices, and what each Axolotl does, might need some changes.

counter.title: Strong bed defense
counter.text: There isn't much counterplay besides your bed defense. It can shred obsidian, so place 2 layers plus wool, since it one-shots stone.

name: Baker
desc: Gain access to health-gain apples, speed-boost pies, and spawn with a knockback baguette!
adv:
Baker always spawns with the Knockback Baguette and can store it in chests for teammates to pick up. Baker can also drop all of its items for teammates, and they have the same capacities.
Apples, Golden Apples and Speed Pies are bought in the shop. Eating an apple slows you down while you eat.
A Golden Apple heals 175 HP in total: 30 instantly, then 5 HP every 0.5 seconds for 15 seconds (145 HP), along with 5% damage reduction until it runs out.

items.name: Health Apple
items.desc: Max 3. Heals 20 HP. Takes 0.8 seconds to eat, and you move slower while eating.

items.name: Speed Pie
items.desc: Unlimited capacity. Gives 100 seconds of speed that increases your movement speed by 27.5% (1.275x). Takes 0.8 seconds to eat.

items.name: Golden Apple
items.desc: Max 3. Takes 1 second to eat, and you move slower while eating. Heals 30 HP instantly, then 5 HP every 0.5 seconds for 15 seconds (145 HP), plus 5% damage reduction until it runs out. 175 HP in total.

items.name: Knockback Baguette
items.desc: Baker always spawns with it. Deals 1 damage and 4 blocks of knockback. Can be stored in chests for teammates to pick up.

balWhy:
For 3 emeralds you are basically unkillable, unless the other team has enchants and gets lucky and rolls static. Coils aren't much of a counter because they aren't mobile. Healing more than double your HP for 3 emeralds is insane, and with the Speed Pie, which outclasses most movement kits, it's a bit crazy.
Suggested changes: keep the healing the same but tick every 0.75s instead of 0.5s, which makes it easier to deal with in fights. Raise the damage reduction by another 5% to make up for it, and nerf the Speed Pie to 1.75x movement instead of 2x.

passives.name: Knockback Baguette
passives.desc: Baker always spawns with the Knockback Baguette and can store it in chests for teammates to pick up.

passives.name: Team Supplies

name: Barbarian
desc: Build rage by damaging enemies. Instead of buying swords, your sword is upgraded when you reach enough rage. You lose all your rage on death. The Emerald Sword is replaced by the Rageblade.
adv:
Barbarian cannot buy swords. You start with a wooden sword and upgrade it by building rage, which you get from dealing damage and from kills. Once upgraded, your sword never goes back to the previous one when you die.

Iron sword: 210

Rageblade: 650

Ranged damage gives 2x less rage than other damage. Killing an enemy gives you around 40 damage worth of rage. You cannot get rage from enemies who respawned within the last 9 seconds.
When you die you lose all your rage and restart the tier you are on.

name: Beekeeper Beatrix
desc: Catch bees around the map to upgrade your Bee Hive. Upgrading your Bee Hive will return additional iron and emeralds.
adv:
Bees spawn around the map, similar to Alchemist's ingredients but not as many, and the amount depends on the map. A bee on the ground disappears 3 minutes after it spawns, and bees pulse every 7 seconds so they are easier to find. Hold the Bee Net to pick a bee up: it goes into your inventory as a separate item, then you put it in a Beehive. You lose your bees when you die, but you keep the net. Bees inside a hive never despawn.
You can place up to 5 Beehives. A hive with 0 bees only produces iron, 1 iron every 10 seconds. The more bees inside, the faster it drops loot, and from 3 bees it can drop diamonds, and from 4 bees it can drop emeralds. Each drop is only 1 resource at a time: either 1 iron, 1 diamond or 1 emerald. After 10 bees a hive doesn't drop any faster. There are no hive upgrades.
Hives have normal block HP and are weak to pickaxes: they break in 5 hits with a wooden pickaxe, 4 with stone, and 2 with iron or diamond. They can also be broken by TNT and fireballs if they aren't covered with ceramic or obsidian.

desc: Summon a mythical falcon to dominate an area. Work in tandem to critically strike your companion's target with your feather light bows

desc: Get assigned bounties for killing certain players in the match. Completing a bounty rewards a random amount of resources.
adv:
A random player in the server is your target. Hunting Time marks your target on the map, but your target also sees your mark, so they know where you are and that they are your target. They can't see the mark if you don't click Hunting Time. You can reroll your target (random) every 60 seconds.

After you get a new bounty you have to wait 20 seconds before you can get another one, and that timer starts when you reroll. So if you reroll and kill your target quickly, you still wait out the 20 seconds. desc: Fortify blocks with extra health and blast protection using the Builder's hammer. Purchase the Hammer from the Item Shop.
adv:
Builder spawns with a Builder Hammer and 8 Stone Bricks. The Stone Bricks are normal, so you still need to upgrade them. With the hammer you can upgrade blocks using iron or emeralds. Upgraded (reinforced) blocks are blast resistant and have 60% more durability, which makes them harder to break.
It takes about 8 TNT to break a single reinforced stone brick, while the other reinforced blocks still get one shot by TNT. Siege TNT still one shots, but it destroys fewer blocks when they are reinforced than when they aren't.
The hammer can also upgrade other kits' items, like Beekeeper Beatrix's Beehives.
The Bridge Printer is bought in the shop. Use the hammer and click the printer source to turn it on or off, and it stretches out blocks (see the Bridge Printer details).

Better armor on the target gives better upgrades. Sometimes a special contract appears on a player with diamond armor or higher, and completing it gives your decay a special effect. name: Cogsworth
desc: Deploy robots that search for generators and collect resources!
adv:
Cogsworth spawns with a Dimmy-X1 bot and the Overclock ability. You can buy as many Dimmy-X1 (50 iron) and Emmy-Z2 (1 emerald) bots as you want, but only 4 of each can be placed at once. Placing a bot takes 2.5 seconds and locks you in place.
Dimmy-X1 goes to the nearest diamond generator and brings the diamonds to your team chest. Emmy-Z2 collects emeralds and puts them in your personal chest. Bots have a 60% chance to double the resources they pick up, and you can also take resources straight off your bots.
Bots move as fast as players, take no knockback, can jump over 1 block gaps, and run away from enemies unless they're waiting for a diamond or emerald to spawn. They glow red on your screen when an enemy is within 8 blocks. They need a bridge to reach a generator, and sometimes the AI walks into the void.
Overclock lasts 5 seconds (20 second cooldown) and makes your bots 1.85x faster. While it's active, every bot deals 4 damage every 0.5 seconds (10 ticks) in an 8 block radius with knockback, and Zaps enemies it hits. The damage stacks, so all 8 bots deal 32 per tick.

strategy.title: Robot coil defense
strategy.text: Place a coil near your bed and cover it with ceramic or obsidian. Stand against the covered coil and place your robots so they clip into it. When enemies come, Overclock deals knockback and insane shred damage to keep them away.

strategy.title: Stack tick damage
strategy.text: Use Fire or Static for even more tick damage.

counter.title: Use projectiles
counter.text: Try to kill Cogsworth with projectiles, since it can't run for cover.

counter.title: Clear the bots first
counter.text: If the robots are on a bed, use a lot of TNT to kill them all before you rush. Rushing without clearing them is a death sentence.

balWhy: Cogsworth does great damage with its robots and gets good loot, since it can duplicate resources from multiple generators. It can be countered if an enemy goes after Cogsworth itself, but that's a bit hard to do.

name: Conqueror
desc: Place banners to empower nearby allies.
adv:
Conqueror can buy 3 banners in the shop for 60 iron each: the Defense Banner, Fire Banner and Heal Banner. You can hold up to 3 of each, but only 1 of each type can be placed at a time.
Banners buff every ally within a 9 block radius and disappear after 30 seconds. They're weak to pickaxes (16 hits with wood, 10 with stone, 7 with iron, 4 with diamond) and can also be destroyed with TNT or fireballs.
The Defense Banner makes you take no knockback. The Fire Banner gives your hits the normal Fire enchant. Both buffs stay for 5 seconds after the banner disappears or you leave its radius. The Heal Banner heals you every second based on your missing HP, so it heals more the lower you are, but it stops as soon as you leave.

strategy.title: Bed breaks
strategy.text: Go with a teammate and place all 3 banners on the bed (Defense, Heal, then Fire). Fight while your teammate breaks the bed, or switch roles if your teammate has a bed breaking kit.

strategy.text: Use the Fire Banner during fights. It's a bit more useful than the Heal Banner.

strategy.title: High HP teammates
strategy.text: Kits with more HP, like Eldertree, get more out of the Heal Banner since it heals a percentage, not a set amount.

counter.text: Get a diamond pickaxe and have your team mine the banner together to break it almost instantly. Break speed upgrades make it even faster.

name: Crocowolf
desc: Being in the vicinity of damage dealt builds bloodlust. Activate Beast Form to temporarily give you enhanced damage, knockback, and movement speed. Dealing damage to non-player entities builds more bloodlust. When your bed breaks you will be given full bloodlust.
adv:
Crocowolf builds Bloodlust from damage dealt near it. Once you have 300 Bloodlust, you can activate Beast Form.
Bloodlust counts the base damage of every hit within 5 blocks of you: your hits, your teammates' hits and your enemies' hits, including hits on you. For example, an iron sword (30 damage) fills it in 10 hits. Hits on NPCs like Diamond Guards and the Titan count double, so you only need half as much. Kills don't give extra Bloodlust, and you lose all of it when you die. When your bed breaks, your bar fills all the way up.
Activating Beast Form heals you 20 HP right away. While transformed you deal 25% more damage from every source (swords, ranged weapons and more), move 27.5% faster (1.275x), and deal 1 block more knockback.
Beast Form slowly drains your Bloodlust, lasting about 12 seconds from a full bar. You have to wait 5 seconds before you can cancel it, and if you cancel early you keep whatever Bloodlust is left (cancel 6 seconds in and you keep about 50%). You can only activate it with a full bar.

It drains your Bloodlust (about 12 seconds from full). You can cancel it after 5 seconds and keep whatever Bloodlust is left. Only works with a full bar.

name: Crypt
desc: Claim souls to build your undead army! Could be unlocked for FREE by completing Crypt's Trials during the Halloween 2022 event.
adv:
Crypt spawns with the Necromancer Staff, which summons your skeleton army. Whenever a player dies, a gravestone appears that you can collect from any distance away (if they died in the void, it shows up near the middle of the map); gravestones never despawn. Hold for 0.1 seconds within 3 blocks to pick one up. You can carry as many as you want, but only 5 skeletons can be out at once (melee and ranged together).
There are 2 kinds of skeletons. Melee skeletons have 150 HP, move at normal speed, and use the sword of the player you killed with that sword's cooldown and 75% of its damage. They hit every enemy bunched up in front of them, unlike a normal sword. Ranged skeletons have 100 HP and stay in place: a bow does 18 damage every 2.5 seconds, a crossbow does 28 and a headhunter does 33, both every 3.5 seconds.
Skeletons get the helmet of the player you killed (iron, diamond or emerald). At minimum they always get a leather helmet and a wood sword or bow. If the player took off their helmet before dying, the skeleton only gets leather. Skeletons last 2 minutes, all die when you die, and use your enchants (except Soul Reaver, which gives you the stack instead).
While holding the staff, you can use Set Target on an enemy within 9 blocks (1 second cooldown) and Recall Skeletons to teleport them all to you (5 second cooldown).

name: Cyber
desc: Deploy and control drones to pickup resources from around the map. Drones can also airdrop primed TNT.
adv:
Cyber can buy a Drone for 40 iron. Equip it to take control and fly it anywhere on the map. The drone can carry a stack of iron, diamonds or emeralds, but only one type at a time (like 10 diamonds, but no iron or emeralds with them).
While you're not flying it, you can load up to 10 TNT into the drone. While flying, press X to drop a TNT, which starts detonating wherever it lands.
The drone has a 490 second battery. When it runs out, the drone explodes (it doesn't do damage) and you have to buy a new one. Stop using the drone to instantly refill the battery.
The drone only has 20 HP and doesn't show a health bar, so it's hard to tell how hurt it is. If Cyber dies, the drone stops completely wherever it is. If the drone is destroyed, whoever killed it gets the loot it was carrying.

It needs a heavy resource buff to be viable, and maybe more defense, like an upgraded drone that's slower and bulkier and swaps the speed boost for an attack.

name: Death Adder
desc: Charge up explosive comets to rain destruction on your enemy's base. Collect alchemy crystals to unlock even stronger abilities!
adv:
Death Adder spawns with the Charge Explosive Comet ability. Alchemy Crystals spawn around the map every so often and despawn after 3 minutes. Collecting them gives you crystals to shoot (your UI shows how many you're holding), and collecting enough levels up your comet. The count resets every level, and it only matters how many you collect, even if you're already full.
Hold the ability to charge a comet, then release to shoot it. Each charge takes 1 second, and the first one has to finish before you can shoot. You can cancel any time, and the ability has a 1 second cooldown. Each shot uses 1 crystal no matter how many charges you use. While charging you move about 50% slower.
The comet deals hit damage, then explodes for around 60 damage, with less damage the farther the explosion is from the target. Neither part has armor penetration. Level 3 unlocks a second charge and level 5 a third; extra charges make the explosion bigger. Block damage maxes out at level 3, which can take obsidian down by about 80%.

name: Dino Tamer Dom
desc: Can purchase a Dino mount. Charge into defenses to knock them down!
adv:
Dino Tamer Dom can buy a Dino for 60 iron. Summoning it takes 2 seconds and slows you down a lot while it happens. Riding it makes you about 20% faster than walking. You keep the Dino when you get off, but you lose it when you die.
While riding, you can use Charge (40 second cooldown). It lasts 3 seconds and fills a bar; the fuller the bar, the more damage the explosion does to blocks. The bar is full after 2 seconds. Ramming a player deals about 85 damage with no armor penetration (about 38 to iron armor). Running into any block during the charge makes it explode and ends the charge. You can't use weapons while charging.
A full charge breaks up to 2 layers of obsidian, but not every block. Against a normal obsidian bed defense (8 obsidian around the bed) it breaks 1-3 blocks depending on how you hit it, and it can't get through 3 layers to expose the bed.

name: Drill
desc: Purchase Drills to deploy on Diamond and Emerald generators. Drills automatically harvest 2x gen resources. Control them to fight off attackers.
adv:
Drill spawns with a Drill and a Tablet. You can buy more Drills for 3 emeralds each and hold as many as you want, but only 4 can be placed on the map at once.
Place a Drill on a diamond or emerald generator to take it over and double its resources: you get 1 of that resource straight into your inventory, and the generator's own drop is stored inside the drill. There's also a 25% chance for an extra diamond or emerald to spawn inside it. You or your teammates can take the stored resources by holding R (Extract Ore).
Drills get stronger as the match goes on: damage goes up at 5 and 10 minutes, and HP goes up at 6:40 and 13:20. They slowly heal themselves over time, and you get a notification when one of your drills takes damage. If an enemy destroys a drill, they get all the loot stored inside it. They attack with a 0.5 second cooldown, but can't hit players standing 2 blocks above them within 3 blocks.
Use the Tablet to control your drills, and press A or D to cycle back and forth between them.

name: Eldertree
desc: Collect tree orbs around the map to increase size and max HP. Cannot buy armor.
adv:
Eldertree can't buy armor. Instead, it grows by collecting tree orbs that spawn around the map, most often near the middle. Walk within 2 blocks of an orb to pick it up automatically. Orbs disappear after 2 minutes and 30 seconds.
Every orb gives you more max HP, makes you bigger, and makes you take 1% less knockback (up and sideways), up to 15% less at 15 orbs. You start at normal player size (2 blocks tall, 1.5 wide). The HP gain shrinks a little with each orb: the first orb gives +30, and by 60 orbs each one gives about +11. You start at 100 HP and reach about 500 HP at 26 orbs and 1,000 HP at 70 orbs.

name: Eldric
desc: Drain health from enemies or sacrifice your health to heal allies. Could be unlocked for FREE by completing Crypt's Coven during the Halloween 2023 event.
adv:
Eldric spawns with the Warlock Staff. Lock onto an enemy within 8 blocks to drain their HP every 0.75 seconds. The damage ramps up the longer you stay attached (+5 over about 8 ticks at 0 stacks) and is higher the closer you are: you deal full damage within about 3 blocks, and damage drops off the farther away you are. A yellow bar warns you between 8 and 10 blocks, and past 10 blocks you detach. The staff ignores 50% of armor.
Every hit heals you about 35% of the damage. If you're already at full HP, that healing turns into shield instead, up to 25.
You can also lock onto a teammate to heal them every tick (3 HP at 0 stacks, 27 at 30 stacks). It costs you 3.5 HP per tick, and they deal 25% more damage while linked.
You get a stack when you kill with the staff, when you get an assist (a teammate gets a kill while you're linked to them or to their target), or by killing NPCs like Diamond Guards. Each stack adds about 1.4 damage per tick and more healing, and the range grows too: at max stacks you can lock on from 12 blocks and stay attached up to 14. Max 30 stacks.

adv:
Void Knight spawns with 90 HP, a Noctium Blade I and the Consume ability. Consume eats 10 resources at a time (0.1 second cooldown), and you level up by consuming resources and dealing sword damage, and every kill counts as 200 damage toward that. Damage to NPCs (like Diamond Guards) and any damage that isn't from your sword only counts 50%. There are 5 forms: Base, Enhanced, Empowered, Corrupt and Chosen. Each form upgrades your blade and gives more damage reduction.
Empowered Form adds Void Decay to your hits: the first hit takes away 10% of the enemy's total HP, and the decay lasts 10 seconds before you need to hit them again. Corrupt Form gives you a 30 HP shield that fully comes back after 15 seconds of not taking damage.
Chosen Form is the last upgrade: Consume is replaced by Void Ascension, your damage reduction goes up to 84%, and you keep the Noctium Blade IV and the shield. Void Ascension gives you 20% more damage on everything (not just your sword) and 30% more health for 15 seconds, with a 60 second cooldown.

strategy.title: Consume everything
strategy.text: Play Void Knight like any other kit, just remember to consume your resources as soon as you get them.

strategy.title: Rush the shield
strategy.text: Once you get the shield upgrade, you are almost unkillable unless someone has emerald armor.

strategy.title: Stack more HP
strategy.text: Try to roll the Forest enchant for even more HP. Void Ascension's extra health works with other HP buffs too, like Star Collector Stella's Vitality Stars.

counter.title: Kill it early
counter.text: Void Knight is really bad early game because of its slow sword speed, so it is easy to kill. Try to get it out of the game before it gets the shield upgrade.

counter.title: Use damage over time
counter.text: If it already has the shield, keep ticking its HP down with damage over time, like Fire.

balWhy: Void Knight is insanely tanky, and you don't have to worry about spending emeralds on gear because you just consume them. Combine Void Ascension's extra HP with other HP buffs like the Forest enchant or Star Collector Stella's Vitality Stars and you are almost unkillable.
